About the weather scene

Illustrations and synthesized ambient sound follow the latest station observation, independent of the selected history dates. Rain scenes use the reported instantaneous rate: light below 2.5 mm/h; moderate to heavy from 2.5 to below 50 mm/h; very heavy to extreme at 50 mm/h and above. These visual bands are not official daily-rainfall warning categories.

Day and night use the observation time and station coordinates. Daytime sky is estimated from solar radiation relative to the sun's elevation; cloud cover is not measured. The starry night scene is illustrative, not confirmation of a clear sky. Missing or stale data pause sound; reduced-motion preferences pause animation. Whooshing wind overlays any weather sound when the latest observed gust exceeds 20 km/h. Sound starts automatically where the browser allows it; otherwise tap Start sound & animation. All cloud scenes use moving cloud layers. Light rain is illustrated as fine drizzle beneath moving stratiform clouds. The night scene includes a moon, stars and occasional meteor showers. Very heavy/extreme rain adds a localized lightning strike about every 8–14 seconds, followed by thunder when sound is enabled. Lightning, thunder and meteors are artistic effects, not station detections.

Solar, UV and peak rain rate records compare daily peaks: their lowest value is the lowest daily peak, not a nighttime minimum. Direction is circular, so use the wind rose instead of numeric min/max. Pressure midpoint values are derived from the daily high and low; they are not reported daily means. Averages of daily means are unweighted; gaps remain missing. Today is a partial day.
